text:
maria_arch: quick follow-up from the RFC — thinking about externalizing fallback decisioning into a small control-plane (separate service) rather than baking complex heuristics into the router. pros/cons?
raj_sre: main cons i see: extra network hop and potential latency tail. also more moving pieces to monitor. :grimacing:
oliver_runtime: don't underestimate the path cost — router is in the hot path. any external call must be <50ms or we need a fallback default.
sophia_ml: +1 on latency constraints. but we can precompute risk signals and push them to a fast cache the router reads, so the control-plane is mainly for policy updates and heavy eval.
maria_arch: exactly — hybrid model: router has a small, fast local policy (cached) and the external controller handles complex scoring + historical signals. idea is keep the fast path simple, heavyweight checks live off-path.
raj_sre: how do we prevent split-brain between local cache and controller? staleness could cause bad rollouts.
maria_arch: TTL + vector clock and a low-cost consistency check. if local cache age > threshold, router falls back to safest variant.
oliver_runtime: propose an explicit timeout/hedge behavior: router calls controller with timeout 40ms. if no response, proceed using local policy and mark request for async telemetry. can we live with that?
sophia_ml: we should also add a probe channel that validates controller decisions against live traffic. small mirror and score drift daily.
maria_arch: interface sketch (config snippet):
```
fallback_control: {
  mode: "hybrid",
  local_cache_ttl_ms: 120,
  controller_timeout_ms: 40,
  safety_thresholds: {err_rate: 0.015, p95_latency_ms: 250},
  probe_fraction: 0.01
}
```
raj_sre: TTL 120ms seems tight for some infra. maybe make it tunable per-region. also add smoothing to thresholds to avoid flip-flop.
maria_arch: yes tunable per-region and per-tenant. add exponential smoothing window in policy.
oliver_runtime: operational requirements:
- clear metrics: decision latency, controller availability, local cache hit rate
- circuit breaker that forces all traffic to safe variant if controller fault > X
- ability for router to accept controller 'advisory' vs 'enforced' decisions
sophia_ml: the advisory vs enforced flag is critical. we can run advisory in staging and then flip enforcement after confidence.
maria_arch: rollout plan idea:
1) controller in staging advisory mode + 1% probe in prod
2) increase probes, enable smoothing, validate drift alerts
3) 10% canary using advisory + operator review
4) flip enforcement for canary paths, ramp to 100%
added checklist: telemetry dashboards, abort button, runbook update.
raj_sre: ops Q: what happens on controller config push failures? do we invalidate local caches or keep old?
maria_arch: keep old until valid config accepted. controller must provide versioned configs; router only switches on validated commit.
oliver_runtime: small implementation note: make the router <-> controller protocol simple (protobuf/gRPC) and keep payloads tiny (decision token + metadata). avoid full request replay.
sophia_ml: also include a debug tracing header so we can track why a decision was made for specific requests.
deploy-bot: controller v0.3 deployed to staging with hybrid mode enabled (probe_fraction=0.01).
maria_arch: thanks — next steps: oliver to prototype proto and timeout semantics, raj to draft SLOs/alerts, sophia to prepare drift eval harness. i'll update RFC with config sketch and rollout checklist.
raj_sre: noted. i'll add ops page + emergency abort steps. :thumbsup:
